item.title: Red States Just Asked the Supreme Court to Kill Abortion Shield Laws
item.description:
FIRST ON FOX — The Supreme Court agreed Thursday to hear a Kentucky church’s fight to build a prayer grotto on its property, taking up a dispute over what constitutes a "substantial burden" on religious exercise under federal land-use law. Ryan Gardner, senior counsel at First Liberty Institute, which represents the Missionaries of St. John the Baptist, told Fox News Digital the implications stretch far beyond the proposed Catholic shrine in Park Hills, Kentucky. "This is a massive case for religious liberty because it has the potential to impact every single zoning law in this country," Gardner told Fox News Digital. item.title: UK is not facing diesel shortage despite fears of Trump export ban, minister says
item.description:
US President Donald Trump held crisis talks over whether to institute a diesel export ban as fuel prices surge nationwide, the Financial Times reported, with one industry figure suggesting a ban was “getting pretty close to movement.” Top Republicans have called on Trump to “ stop the bleeding ” as soaring prices rattle the party a month before the midterm elections, though some cabinet members, including the energy secretary, have argued against a ban. Diesel prices could remain elevated for a year, according to a new survey of oil and gas executives . The White House said this week that Trump will campaign with an embattled Republican senator in Alaska, where gas prices have topped $10 per gallon and, in remote communities, approached $30 a gallon . — Brendan Ruberry

item.title: California gubernatorial candidates face off in debate
item.description:
The first and probably only face-to-face debate between the two candidates for California governor Wednesday night established its pattern right off the bat . The two CNN anchors who conducted the event in Burbank, Jake Tapper and Dana Bush, would raise one of the state’s most pressing issues and seek responses from Democrat Xavier Becerra and Republican Steve Hilton . Hilton would blame decades of Democratic political control for causing, or at least not fixing, the problem. Becerra would repeatedly shift the blame to Donald Trump, well aware that the president is very unpopular in the state. “All you say is Trump, Trump, Trump,” Hilton said when the issue was immigration. “Trump, Trump, Trump,” Becerra responded. So it went for an hour and a dozen issues. Hilton, who trails Becerra by double digits in the polls and has no chance of becoming governor, actually put forth some policy…

item.title: Judge denies motion asking for Lindsay Clancy to be found not guilty due to lack of evidence
item.description:
A Massachusetts judge has rejected Lindsay Clancy’s defense request for a not-guilty finding, ruling that prosecutors presented sufficient evidence for a jury to consider the charges in the deaths of her three children: 5-year-old Cora, 3-year-old Dawson, and 8-month-old Callan. item.title: Why Trump’s Crypto Business Wants to Become a Bank
item.description:
In a move that Sen. Elizabeth Warren has decried as a “clear conflict of interest and corruption,” one of the Trump family’s most lucrative businesses is on its way to becoming a bank. And it’s set to be regulated by a government entity whose leader was appointed by, you guessed it, President Donald Trump. In August, the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency—one of three major bank regulators in the United States—declared that Trump’s controversial crypto company, World Liberty Financial, could begin the process of establishing itself as a bank. It’s a complicated regulatory move that not only creates a new level of conflict of interest for the president and his family, but demonstrates just how drastically Trump has reshaped federal government policy in an effort to embrace his fellow crypto entrepreneurs. item.title: From Super Bowl champ to master architect: Mike Tomlin’s sprawling Minecraft city is magnificent
item.description:
The former Pittsburgh Steelers head coach took 12 years to build a city filled with stadiums, skyscrapers and bespoke homes. It is a marvel We may finally have cracked the case as to why the Pittsburgh Steelers stagnated so much over the final years of Mike Tomlin’s tenure as head coach: he was focused on virtual urban planning. I’m kidding, of course. It’s good when people in high-pressure jobs have creative hobbies. Count this writer (and his interior designer wife) among those who were gobsmacked on Wednesday night by Tomlin’s reveal of a 12-year-long project in Minecraft, the world-building game. Tomlin had teased that during his coaching career, he took up Minecraft city-building as a way to connect with his young children. We have now seen the fruits of that labor, and they are magnificent . Look my my works, Terry Bradshaw, and despair. Continue reading...

item.title: France unveils cost-cutting budget amid protests
item.description:
The French government is seeking €54 billion in savings in its 2027 budget proposal, as it faces pressure over its ballooning public debt. But it's likely to face opposition, especially on proposals that would cap pension increases. Meanwhile, protests by high school students over resources and conditions in classrooms have spread across the country, with the budget likely to further inflame tensions.

item.title: Open Thread
item.description:
Time is not on Iran’s side. While much could still happen to disrupt America’s progress in the war, the Iran strategy being pursued by the Donald Trump administration has given it the upper hand over Tehran. You can see signs of that momentum in all three parts of the administration’s strategy: the blockade of Iranian ports, expanded sanctions, and escort operations in the Strait of Hormuz. Imposing the blockade back in April was President Trump’s best decision of the war. He briefly lifted the blockade as part of the memorandum of understanding (MOU), a mistake that allowed Iran to benefit from a significant influx of cash, but the blockade again appears to be completely effective. Iran used to export about two million barrels of oil per day through the Strait of Hormuz.
